Download raw data from public sources

18 July 2025

Source: vignettes/download.Rmd
download.Rmd

Load packages

library(here)
library((janitor)
library(tidyverse)

STEP1 - Opcion A: Download data from URL

Combined antibiogram dataset

You can download the antibiogram files from ENA browser, BV-BRC, and NCBI using the reference file available on Zenodo, published on July 4, 2025 (version 4).

# Define URL and local destination
anti_url <- "https://zenodo.org/records/15809334/files/antibiograms.tsv.zip"
# Replace "inst/extdata" with the actual path to your folder
targetfile <- here("inst/extdata", "antibiograms.tsv.zip") # <- Change this to your own directory

# Download the compressed file
download.file(url = anti_url, destfile = targetfile, mode = "wb")

# Unzip the .zip file
unzip(targetfile, exdir = "inst/extdata")

# Import the data into R
antibiograms_metadata <- readr::read_tsv(here("inst/extdata","antibiograms.tsv"))  # <- Specify the directory path

You can compress the file to .gz format before loading it into R. The read_tsv() function supports reading .gz-compressed files directly.

# Compress the file to .gz format
original_file <- here("inst/extdata", "antibiograms.tsv")
gz_file <- here("inst/extdata", "antibiograms.tsv.gz")
R.utils::gzip(original_file, destname = gz_file, overwrite = TRUE)

# Read the .tsv.gz file into R
antibiograms_metadata <- readr::read_tsv(here("inst/extdata", "antibiograms.tsv.gz"))

We recommend simplifying column formats using the janitor package and standardizing column names as shown below.

# Clean antibiogram metadata
antibiograms_db <- antibiograms_metadata %>%
  # Standardizes column names: converts them to lowercase,
  # replaces spaces and special characters with underscores
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  # Renames the columns
  rename(
    accession = reads,
    scientific_name_Antibiogram = species
  )

CAMDA training dataset 

# Define the raw URL
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EveliaCoss/AMRdb/devel/inst/extdata/training_dataset.csv"

# Destination filename
dest <- "training_dataset.csv"

# Download the file
download.file(url, dest, mode = "wb")

# Load the data
training_metadata <- read.csv(dest, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Rename species
training_metadata_db <- training_metadata %>%
  mutate(scientific_name_CAMDA = paste(genus, species, sep = " "))

CAMDA test dataset 

# Define the raw URL
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EveliaCoss/AMRdb/devel/inst/extdata/testing_template.csv"

# Destination filename
dest <- "testing_template.csv"

# Download the file
download.file(url, dest, mode = "wb")

# Load the data
test_metadata <- read.csv(dest, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Rename species
test_metadata_db <- test_metadata %>%
  mutate(scientific_name_CAMDA = paste(genus, species, sep = " ")) %>%
  mutate(antibiotic = if_else(antibiotic == "tetracycline", "TET", antibiotic))

STEP1 - Opcion B: Download data from packages

Combined antibiogram dataset

Download antibiogram files from ENA browser, BV-BRC, and NCBI via the Zenodo reference (version 4, July 4, 2025).

library(AMRdb)

dir <- system.file("extdata", package="AMRdb")
# Read the .tsv.gz file into R
antibiograms_metadata <- readr::read_tsv(file.path(dir, "antibiograms.tsv.gz"))

CAMDA training dataset 

dir <- system.file("extdata", package="AMRdb")
training_metadata <- readr::read_csv(file.path(dir, "training_dataset.csv"))
# Rename species
training_metadata_db <- training_metadata %>%
  mutate(scientific_name_CAMDA = paste(genus, species, sep = " "))
# Rows: 6144 Columns: 16── Column

CAMDA test dataset

The data were provided by CAMDA as part of the 2025 challenge focused on phenotype and MIC prediction using publicly available datasets from 9 bacterial species. However, we have identified that the test dataset includes duplicated entries or information already present in the training dataset. This redundancy may affect model evaluation and should be carefully examined during preprocessing.

# Load CAMDA test dataset
dir <- system.file("extdata", package="AMRdb")
# Read the .csv file into R
test_metadata <- readr::read_csv(file.path(dir, "testing_template.csv"))

# Rename species
test_metadata_db <- test_metadata %>%
  mutate(scientific_name_CAMDA = paste(genus, species, sep = " ")) %>%
  mutate(antibiotic = if_else(antibiotic == "tetracycline", "TET", antibiotic))
# Rows: 5345 Columns: 6── Column

NCBI information 

# Read the .csv file into R
dir <- system.file("extdata", package="AMRdb")
sra_metadata_db <- readr::read_csv(file.path(dir, "sra-metadata.csv") %>%
  # Standardizes column names: converts them to lowercase,
  # replaces spaces and special characters with underscores
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  # Select columns
  select(run, library_strategy, library_selection, library_source, platform,
         model, bio_project, bio_sample, scientific_name) %>%
  # Renames columns
  rename(accession = run, scientific_name_complete = scientific_name)

# Reduce name
sra_metadata_db$scientific_name_NCBI <- word(sra_metadata_db$scientific_name_complete, 1, 2)

Genome taxonomy database (GTDB)

The information extracted from the Genome Taxonomy Database (GTDB) is linked to the accession IDs provided in both the CAMDA training and test datasets

dir <- system.file("extdata", package="AMRdb")
# test information
test_gtdb_result <- readr::read_csv(file.path(dir, "test.ani.csv"))
# training information
train_gtdb_result <- readr::read_csv(file.path(dir, "train.ani.csv"))
